evals.name: Application OutOfSync and Degraded
evals.prompt: My Application podinfo in the apps namespace is showing OutOfSync and Degraded. Debug it.
expectations: Retrieves the Application resource and shows its sync and health status
Identifies the sync status as OutOfSync and health as Degraded
Checks status conditions for errors (ComparisonError, SyncError)
Checks operation state for last sync result and error messages
Identifies which resources are out of sync or unhealthy
Inspects the unhealthy managed resources (Deployments, Pods)
Checks pod logs or events for failing containers

Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.

Every recommended action states its IMPACT — what else is affected if someone acts on it (components that restart, other Applications or tenants affected, whether anything is deleted, and any ordering dependency on another recommendation) — not only its priority. 'Impact: nothing else is affected' counts; omitting the impact entirely does not. An impact reasoned from manifests rather than verified against a cluster must say so.

evals.name: Canary Rollout stuck at step 2
evals.prompt: The canary rollout for frontend in production namespace is stuck at step 2. Figure out why.
expectations: Retrieves the Rollout and identifies its current phase
Identifies the current step index and what step 2 is
Checks pause conditions (manual pause vs analysis-driven)
Inspects associated AnalysisRuns if analysis is involved

Checks the AnalysisRun's metric results and measurements, and reports the measurement phase actually observed rather than assuming a failure. An analysis still in Running with an in-flight measurement is a different diagnosis from one that returned Failed, and the answer must show which it is (phase, measurement count, or the underlying job/pod state) before recommending anything.

Checks spec.strategy.canary.trafficRouting and reports what it finds. If no traffic routing is configured, says so explicitly and explains the consequence — the canary weight is approximated by replica counts rather than a real traffic split, so setWeight: 20 means pods, not 20% of requests. Reporting the absence with that consequence is a full pass; silently omitting the check is not.
Compares stable vs canary ReplicaSets and pod status

Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.

evals.name: Argo CD installation health check
evals.prompt: Check if Argo CD is properly installed on my cluster and report the status.
expectations: Checks for argoproj.io CRDs on the cluster
Identifies the Argo CD namespace (argocd or openshift-gitops)
Lists pods and their status in the Argo CD namespace
Checks core component health (server, repo-server, application-controller)
Reports the Argo CD version
Inspects configuration (argocd-cm or ArgoCD CR)

Reports any unhealthy components with diagnostic details, citing for each one the observation that establishes it (pod phase and restart count, a CSV/InstallPlan condition, or a CRD field value). Claiming a component is down while output in the same answer shows it Running is a fail.
Produces a structured status report

If an operator upgrade or reconcile is reported as blocked, names the specific blocking object and field rather than asserting it generally — for example the failing InstallPlan and the CRD conversion-webhook setting it failed on, not merely 'the operator is unhealthy'.

evals.name: ApplicationSet not generating expected Applications
evals.prompt: My ApplicationSet team-apps in the openshift-gitops namespace uses a git directory generator but isn't creating any Application resources for the new service directories I added. Debug it.
expectations: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and checks its status.conditions
Identifies the generator type (git directory) and its configuration (repoURL, directories path pattern)
Lists currently generated Applications and cross-references against what's expected
Checks the applicationset-controller logs for generator errors
Identifies a likely cause (path pattern mismatch, repo access, or an exclude rule)

Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.

evals.name: ApplicationSet RollingSync stuck on production step
evals.prompt: Our ApplicationSet uses a RollingSync strategy across staging and production. Staging has been updated but production apps haven't started syncing. Why?
expectations: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and inspects spec.strategy.rollingSync.steps
Identifies which step/matchExpressions group production falls into
Checks whether the staging step's maxUpdate requirement and health gate have been satisfied
Debugs the staging Applications' health status, since an unhealthy staging app blocks progression to the next step
Explains how RollingSync blocks progression on unhealthy or unsynced apps in the current step

Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.

Every recommended action states its IMPACT — what else is affected if someone acts on it (components that restart, other Applications or tenants affected, whether anything is deleted, and any ordering dependency on another recommendation) — not only its priority. 'Impact: nothing else is affected' counts; omitting the impact entirely does not. An impact reasoned from manifests rather than verified against a cluster must say so.

evals.name: Blue-green rollout stuck at preview, never promotes
evals.prompt: The blue-green rollout for checkout-api in namespace prod is sitting at the preview stage and has not promoted. autoPromotionEnabled is false. The team expected it to analyze automatically. Debug it.
expectations: Retrieves the Rollout and identifies strategy.blueGreen configuration
Checks autoPromotionEnabled and explains that false requires manual promotion, not automatic analysis
Checks for prePromotionAnalysis templates and their status if configured
Inspects previewService and activeService configuration for correctness
Distinguishes blue-green behavior from canary (no step-based automatic progression)

Produces a report with root cause and recommendations. Every root cause asserted is backed by the specific observation that establishes it (a field value, pod phase, restart count, condition, or log line actually shown). A cause asserted with no supporting output, or contradicted by output shown elsewhere in the same answer, fails this expectation even if it is plausible and well written.

evals.name: Ambiguous debug request with multiple Argo CD instances
evals.prompt: Something's wrong with Argo CD on this cluster but I don't know which instance — we have more than one. Check what's going on.
expectations: Detects multiple Argo CD instances (multiple namespaces with argocd-labeled pods or multiple ArgoCD CRs)
Lists all detected instances with their namespaces
Asks the user which instance to investigate, or investigates all and clearly separates findings per instance
Does not silently pick one instance without disclosing the ambiguity

Produces a report structured per instance, naming each Argo CD instance found and stating that instance's own findings under it. A single flat report that merges findings across instances, or that names only one instance when several exist, fails this expectation.

evals.name: Suspended Application reported as broken
evals.prompt: My Application billing-service in namespace finance shows as Suspended and the team thinks it's broken. Debug it.
expectations: Retrieves the Application and identifies health.status as Suspended
Explains that Suspended reflects an intentionally paused resource (e.g. a paused CronJob or Rollout), not a failure

Inspects the underlying managed resource and states what is suspended, citing the field that shows it (for example a Rollout's spec.paused or a CronJob's spec.suspend) rather than inferring it from the Application's aggregate health.
Does not treat Suspended as an error requiring remediation unless the user confirms it's unintended

Produces a report that separates the intentional suspension from any genuine problem found alongside it, saying explicitly which is which. Reporting only the suspension when live output shows a real failure, or treating the suspension itself as the failure, fails this expectation.

Reports the suspended workload's ACTUAL readiness from live output — pod phase and restart count, and whether the Services have endpoints — instead of assuming the pause is the only thing happening. Suspended health can mask an unrelated failure, so an explanation of why the workload is not Available that is not backed by shown output is a fail.

evals.name: Multi-source Application with one failing source
evals.prompt: My Application platform-ui uses multiple sources — a Helm chart and a separate values repo. It's OutOfSync and I don't know which source is the problem.
expectations: Detects the Application uses spec.sources[] (multi-source), not spec.source
Iterates every entry in spec.sources[] individually, checking repoURL, targetRevision, path, and Helm valueFiles for each
Identifies which specific source is failing (e.g. wrong values file path, inaccessible repo, or bad targetRevision)
Does not treat a multi-source Application as if it were single-source

Produces a report naming WHICH source is at fault — by index AND repoURL, not just 'a source' — and the concrete fix. Must distinguish the source Argo CD's error blames (the one being rendered) from the source that actually lacks the file, rather than only repeating 'source N of 2' from the error text.

evals.name: Operator OLM Triage
evals.prompt: The OpenShift GitOps operator seems degraded after a recent upgrade. The controller pods are not running the expected version. Investigate.
expectations: Runs `oc get csv` (not `oc get argocd`) to determine the installed operator version and reports the CSV name, version string, and phase (e.g. Succeeded, Replacing, or Failed)

Runs `oc get subscriptions.operators.coreos.com` (fully-qualified, not bare `subscription`) in the operator namespace and reports the channel (e.g. gitops-1.14) and installPlanApproval (Automatic or Manual)
Runs `oc get installplan` in the operator namespace and reports the phase of each InstallPlan; if any is not Complete, identifies it by name and states the blocking condition message

Extracts the container image from a running controller pod (via `oc get pod -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[*].image}'` or equivalent) and compares it to the version declared in the CSV; states whether they match or diverge, citing both values
Retrieves the last 20–50 lines of the operator pod logs and cites any error-level or fatal-level log line verbatim rather than summarizing it

evals.name: RBAC Sync Failure Remediation
evals.prompt: My Application payment-api in namespace openshift-gitops fails to sync with a 'forbidden' error. It cannot create Deployments in the payment namespace. Help me fix it.
expectations: Retrieves the Application using `applications.argoproj.io` (fully-qualified) and quotes the exact SyncError condition message containing 'forbidden' from `.status.conditions`
Identifies the service account name from the error message (e.g. `system:serviceaccount:openshift-gitops:openshift-gitops-argocd-application-controller`) and states it explicitly
Names the specific missing permission triple: verb (`create`), resource (`deployments`), API group (`apps`), and target namespace (`payment`) — all four extracted from the error message, not guessed

Produces a concrete YAML manifest (RoleBinding or ClusterRoleBinding) that references the identified service account by name and namespace, the target namespace, and a roleRef; the YAML must be syntactically valid and contain no `<placeholder>` for the service account fields that were already identified
States explicitly that the fix should not be applied without user approval, using language like 'review before applying' or 'apply after confirmation' — not just presenting the YAML silently

evals.name: Progressive Sync Stuck
evals.prompt: I have an ApplicationSet using RollingSync strategy with 3 waves. Wave 1 completed but wave 2 never starts. What's wrong?
expectations: Retrieves the ApplicationSet using `applicationsets.argoproj.io` (fully-qualified) and reports the `spec.strategy.type` value (RollingSync) and the number of steps defined in `spec.strategy.rollingSync.steps`

Lists the Applications generated by the ApplicationSet (via label selector `argocd.argoproj.io/application-set-name=<name>`) and reports each one's sync status and health status, distinguishing wave 1 (healthy) from wave 2+ (not syncing)

Inspects the ArgoCD CR or application-controller pod args/env for the `--enable-progressive-syncs` flag and states whether it is present or absent — citing the specific field checked (e.g. `spec.controller.env` or the StatefulSet's container args)
Identifies the absent `--enable-progressive-syncs` flag as the root cause and explains that without it the controller ignores the RollingSync strategy entirely

Provides the specific ArgoCD CR patch or controller env entry to add the flag, e.g. adding `ARGOCD_APPLICATIONSET_CONTROLLER_ENABLE_PROGRESSIVE_SYNCS=true` to `spec.controller.env` or adding `--enable-progressive-syncs` to extra args

evals.name: Controller CrashLoop Remediation
evals.prompt: Argo CD applications are not being reconciled. The controller seems to be crashing. Diagnose and fix.
expectations: Runs `oc get pods` with a label selector for the application-controller (e.g. `app.kubernetes.io/component=application-controller`) and reports the pod name, STATUS column value (e.g. CrashLoopBackOff), RESTARTS count, and AGE

Retrieves the controller pod logs (via `oc logs`) and quotes the specific error-level or fatal-level log line that caused the crash — e.g. 'rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted' or 'OOMKilled' — rather than paraphrasing it

Maps the quoted log line to a root cause: ResourceExhausted → Redis/repo-server gRPC message size limit or cache overflow; OOMKilled → container memory limit too low; specific error code cited, not a generic 'the controller crashed'

Proposes a specific remediation that matches the diagnosed cause — e.g. for ResourceExhausted: increase `ARGOCD_APP_STATE_CACHE_EXPIRATION` or Redis maxmemory, or increase `ARGOCD_GRPC_MAX_RECV_MSG_SIZE`; for OOM: patch the controller container resources.limits.memory — and provides the exact `oc patch` command or ArgoCD CR field to change

States the blast radius: which components restart when the fix is applied (e.g. 'this restarts the application-controller StatefulSet; existing Applications are not deleted but reconciliation pauses for ~30s during rollout')

evals.name: Namespace-Scoped Instance Limitation
evals.prompt: I created a namespace-scoped ArgoCD instance in team-a-gitops namespace but it cannot manage resources in team-b namespace. Why?
expectations: Retrieves the ArgoCD CR in `team-a-gitops` and identifies whether it is namespace-scoped by checking for `spec.sourceNamespaces` or the absence of a cluster-scoped role, and states the finding (e.g. 'this instance is namespace-scoped — it has no ClusterRoleBinding and spec.sourceNamespaces is either absent or does not include team-b')

Explains the specific mechanism: namespace-scoped ArgoCD instances use Roles (not ClusterRoles) and can only watch/manage resources in namespaces listed in `spec.sourceNamespaces` or labeled with `argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by=<instance-namespace>` — and that `team-b` has neither
Runs `oc get namespace team-b -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels}'` (or equivalent) and reports whether the `argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by` label is present and what value it has

Provides two concrete fix options: (a) label the target namespace with `oc label namespace team-b argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by=team-a-gitops` and add `team-b` to `spec.sourceNamespaces`, or (b) use a cluster-scoped instance — and explains the trade-off (tenant isolation vs. broader access)

Notes that adding a namespace to a namespace-scoped instance also requires RBAC: the instance's service account needs a Role+RoleBinding in `team-b` granting the permissions it needs to manage resources there
